seal.statement: A successful harness image build (test/distributed/harness/docker-provider.js buildImage, the one build step every lab scenario and cone run uses per docker host for distributed-db:test) retires the image its tag named before the build: it records that id before building, and after the build removes it only when it is now untagged and no container, running or stopped, uses it, never forced. It touches nothing else - no prune, no other dangling image, never a tagged image (pinned product images, redis/node/distroless/pd/postgres bases) - and records the outcome as a typed operation event (recorded, removed, kept-in-use, kept-tagged, kept-remove-failed, kept-unverified, none). A step it cannot verify keeps the image, and retirement never fails the build.

text: New test/distributed/harness/docker-image-retirement.js (imageIdOf, retirePreviousImage, RETIREMENT outcomes). test/distributed/harness/docker-provider.js buildImage records the id its tag names before the build as an image.retire-previous 'recorded' event and, after a completed build, removes that image only when it is now untagged and no container (all: true) uses it, never forced, emitting the outcome (removed, kept-in-use, kept-tagged, kept-remove-failed, kept-unverified, none) with previousId, currentId and detail; it never throws and never touches another image. R17, owner scripts/lab (lab fleet readiness): lab fleet should report each host's docker disk headroom (docker system df and free space under the docker root) as a readiness fact, so a host whose disk is full is refused for placement before an image build fails there. adam-laptop's 30 GB root partition reached 100% with 86 untagged distributed-db:test builds this morning and broke a lab run; scripts/lab/certification-preflight.js already measures free space under the docker root for certification builds, which is the measurement to reuse. Also not repaired here: the untagged builds already on other hosts; this change only stops new ones from accumulating, one retirement per build.
